title: A study to find how well NS-863 works and how safe it is in participants with pulmonary hypertension related to interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD)
official: A Phase 2, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Dose Finding Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Orally Administered NS-863 in Participants with Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with Interstitial Lung Disease (PH-ILD)
summary: Main objective: To investigate the efficacyof NS-863 compared with placebo by analyzing pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) in participants with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD)
conditions: Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with Interstitial Lung Disease (PH-ILD)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Ability to provide written informed consent prior to participation in the trial, which includes the ability to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form (ICF). Participants must be able to read, comprehend, and write at a level sufficient to complete trial-related materials
2. Adult male or female participants 18 (19 years in South Korea) to 80 years of age at the time the ICF is signed
3. A confirmed diagnosis of the following WHO Group 3 PH  based on HRCT imaging, which demonstrates the following evidence of ILD performed within 6 months prior to starting the Treatment Period:     a. ILD     b. CPFE: only allowed for participants with 15% or less emphysema, and the extent of the ILD must be greater than that of the emphysema Participants may have any form of ILD (including IIP, IPF, and connective tissue disease) or CPFE
4. Results of the RHC within 35 days prior to Day 1 and meet all of the following criteria:    a. PVR >4 WU    b.Pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) or left ventricle end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) ≤15 mm Hg    c.mPAP >20 mm Hg
5. 6MWD ≥100 and ≤500 meters repeated twice during the Screening Period or Day 1 prior to the first treatment administration (measured at least 4 hours apart), and both values are within 15% of each other (calculated from the highest value)
6. Baseline FVC <70% (only for participants with connective tissue disease).
7. Able to complete the scheduled visits and follow the instructions of the investigator. For the full list of the inclusion criteria, please refer to the study protocol.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Have a diagnosis of PAH or PH for reasons other than WHO Group 3 PH-ILD as outlined in inclusion criterion 3
2. Other concurrent disease and/or medical condition that, in the judgment of the investigator, may put the participant at risk or may influence the results of the trial or the participant’s ability to complete the entire duration of the trial. For the full list of the exclusion criteria, please refer to the study protocol.
3. Have evidence of clinically significant left-sided heart disease, as defined by:     a. PAWP >15 mm Hg     b. LVEF <40%         Notes: Participants with abnormal LV function attributable entirely to impaired LV filling due to the effects of RV overload (ie, RV hypertrophy and/or dilatation) will not be excluded
4. Receiving > 6 L/min of oxygen supplementation by any mode of delivery at rest at baseline
5. History of clinically significant (per investigator’s judgment) drug or alcohol abuse disorder within the last 6 months
6. Have mental disorders or other conditions that make it difficult to follow the protocol
7. History of calculus urinary
8. History of acute kidney injury within 12 weeks prior to the start of the Screening Visit
9. Participants who have hematuria (>5 RBC/hpf) or proteinuria (urine albumin creatinine ratio [UACR] >150 mg/g or urine protein creatinine ratio [UPCR] >400 mg/g) at the Screening Visit
10. Initiation of pulmonary or cardiac rehabilitation within 12 weeks prior to baseline
11. Life expectancy is less than 6 months
12. Have diseases or symptoms that limit evaluation of 6MWT (eg, peripheral vascular disease, musculoskeletal disorders, and obesity)
13. Current cigarette or e-cigarette smokers or those who have quit within the past 6 months, with a history of ≥20 pack-years smoking
14. Participants who are pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the time of trial participation
15. Use of dual platelet inhibitor therapy
16. Severe acute or chronic medical or laboratory abnormality that may increase the risk associated with trial participation or trial treatment administration (eg, history of intracranial hemorrhage, bleeding events within 6 months prior to baseline) or absolute neutrophil count < 1 x 109/L or platelet count < 50 x 109/L at screening
17. Known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-positive status
18. Active hepatitis due to hepatitis B virus or hepatitis C virus
19. The investigator has judged the participant as unwilling or unable to comply with the protocol
